query: 2026 European Aquatics Junior Swimming Championships Munich July 7-12 2026 detailed event schedule. How many individual and relay gold-medal final events are contested on each day - day 1 (July 7), day 2 (July 8), day 3 (July 9) versus days 4-6? What is the total number of gold-medal events over the full 6-day meet?
answer:
Report delivered above. Headline numbers:

**Per-day gold-medal events:** Day 1 = **3** (1 individual + 2 relay) · Day 2 = **8** (7+1) · Day 3 = **6** (5+1) · Day 4 = **8** (7+1) · Day 5 = **5** (4+1) · Day 6 = **12** (10+2)

**Days 1–3 = 17 golds** (40.5%) vs. **Days 4–6 = 25 golds** (59.5%). **Full meet = 42** (34 individual + 8 relay).

Confidence is high: every day was verified twice over — once against the official Information Bulletin programme published 24 Feb 2026, and again against independent post-meet recaps for each of the six days — and the six daily figures sum to exactly the 42 total Wikipedia states from the event list, so no event can be mis-assigned between days without breaking the sum.

The one thing worth flagging for whatever this feeds: Day 1's count of 3 is unusually low and is structural, not incidental. Because the 50/100/200 events all run heats → semis → finals, day 1's evening session is 7 semifinals plus only the events that skip semis — the women's 400 IM and the two 4×100 free relays. Any reasoning that assumes golds are spread evenly across days (7 per day) would be badly wrong at both ends: day 1 has 3, day 6 has 12.

key_facts: The 2026 European Aquatics Junior Swimming Championships were held 7-12 July 2026 at the Olympia Schwimmhalle (1972 Olympic swimming hall) in Munich Olympic Park, Germany - the 52nd edition and Germany's first time hosting in 40 years.
The full 6-day meet contested exactly 42 gold-medal events: 34 individual finals + 8 relay finals. Wikipedia decomposes this as 20 boys' events + 20 girls' events + 2 mixed events.
Day 1 (Tue 7 July) awarded only 3 golds: 1 individual final (Women's 400 IM) + 2 relay finals (W and M 4x100 Freestyle). The rest of the evening session was 7 semifinals.
Day 2 (Wed 8 July) awarded 8 golds: 7 individual (W/M 200 free, W/M 50 back, W/M 50 breast, M 200 fly) + 1 relay (Mixed 4x100 Free).
Day 3 (Thu 9 July) awarded 6 golds: 5 individual (W 1500 free, M 200 IM, W 50 free, W 100 fly, M 1500 free) + 1 relay (W 4x200 Free).
Day 4 (Fri 10 July) awarded 8 golds: 7 individual (M 100 fly, M 200 breast, M 50 free, W 200 breast, M 200 back, W 200 back, M 400 IM) + 1 relay (Mixed 4x100 Medley).

Day 5 (Sat 11 July) awarded 5 golds: 4 individual (W 200 fly, W 100 free, M 800 free, W 800 free) + 1 relay (M 4x200 Free). Swimming World explicitly reported 'There were five finals scheduled for the session'.

Day 6 (Sun 12 July) awarded 12 golds: 10 individual (W 200 IM, M/W 100 back, M/W 100 breast, M 100 free, W/M 50 fly, W/M 400 free) + 2 relays (W and M 4x100 Medley). No semifinals were held on the final day.
Days 1-3 combined: 17 gold-medal events (13 individual + 4 relay), or 40.5% of the meet. Days 4-6 combined: 25 gold-medal events (21 individual + 4 relay), or 59.5% of the meet.

The schedule is heavily back-loaded because 50m/100m/200m events use a heats-semifinals-finals format. Day 1's only medal events are those that bypass semifinals: the women's 400 IM (direct final) and the two 4x100 free relays.

Cumulative golds awarded: 3 after day 1 (7.1%), 11 after day 2 (26.2%), 17 after day 3 (40.5%), 25 after day 4 (59.5%), 30 after day 5 (71.4%), 42 after day 6 (100%). Day 6 alone carries 28.6% of all golds.
Sessions ran heats at 09:00 and finals at 18:00 local time (CEST) on every one of the six days.

599 athletes competed. Largest delegations: Italy 40, Neutral Athletes (AIN) 39, Germany 37 (host), France 31, Spain/Great Britain/Poland 24 each, Turkiye 21, Hungary 20. 18 nations/delegations won medals.
The programme published in the official Information Bulletin dated 24 February 2026 was executed exactly as published - post-meet recaps for all six days match the bulletin day for day.
Day 1 golds: W 400 IM - Amalie Smith (GBR) 4:35.32 championship record; W 4x100 free - Great Britain 3:37.35 European junior record; M 4x100 free - Neutral Athletes 3:12.75 world junior record.

The official European Aquatics mini-site 'Schedule & Results' page publishes the programme only as two images under a 'TO BE ANNOUNCED SOON' heading, yielding no machine-readable schedule text; the Information Bulletin PDF is the authoritative textual primary source.
The companion EA Junior Artistic Swimming Championships ran 30 June - 4 July 2026 at the same Munich venue, immediately preceding the swimming meet.
The meet was long course (50m), with age brackets of girls 14-17 and boys 15-18.
